title.narrative: Access to Justice & Legal Protection for Refugees & Vulnerable Communities in JO
NRC Jordan - Support for legal documentation

description.narrative:
The proposed intervention has the following overall objective:
"To strengthen the ability of refugees, particularly Syrians, and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women, children and legally excluded groups, to exercise their rights and reduce legal vulnerability through gender responsive legal protection services, empowered local actors, and accessible, accountable justice institutions."
The programme is structured around three interlinked sub-objectives, each corresponding to one or more outcomes:
Sub-Objective 1: Strengthening access to reliable legal information and referral services for refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women, by enhancing the capacity of local organisations and community-based actors through coordinated capacity strengthening, knowledge sharing, and system-level improvements. This sub-objective is expected to deliver two outcomes: (1.1) improved knowledge and understanding of legal rights and available remedies among refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly women; and (1.2) strengthened capacity of community-based organisations to effectively deliver legal information and referral services to refugees and vulnerable Jordanians.
Sub-Objective 2: Enhance access to justice for refugees and vulnerable Jordanians by delivering targeted legal counselling, assistance and evidence-based policy engagement that address complex documentation, civil status, housing, land and property, and return-related legal challenges, with a focus on women and legally excluded groups. This sub-objective is expected to deliver two outcomes: (2.1) refugees and vulnerable Jordanians obtain or exercise their rights through legal aid support; and (2.2) policies, practices or behaviours are positively influenced through evidence-based advocacy and engagement.
Sub-Objective 3: Improve the accessibility and responsiveness of Jordan's justice institutions by supporting the Ministry of Justice to institutionalise, operationalise, and digitalise inclusive fast track small claims procedures and strengthen the capacity of justice actors to apply them consistently. This sub-objective is expected to deliver one outcome: (3.1) improved efficiency and accessibility of the Jordanian justice system through strengthened small-claims procedures and enhanced capacity of justice actors.
The programme's intended impact is a more accessible, inclusive, gender responsive and resilient justice ecosystem in Jordan, where refugees and vulnerable Jordanians, particularly those with heightened legal vulnerability, experience strengthened protection, reduced legal insecurity, and improved pathways towards durable solutions.
